blind_solve.my_reasoning: A firm non-fluctuant mass persisting after treated lactational mastitis needs structural characterisation first, and ultrasound is the imaging modality of choice in a lactating breast to separate a solid inflammatory phlegmon from a drainable collection.

Intermediate clinical probability calls for imaging rather than the operating room or bare observation, and in a non-pregnant man with a body mass index of 34 kg/m2 contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the modality that performs best.

Computed tomography shows uncomplicated appendicitis with no perforation, abscess or phlegmon in a physiologically stable adult with no anaesthetic or laparoscopic contraindication, so appendectomy on this admission is the standard of care.

Two discrete depressive episodes with full inter-episode recovery, collateral history negative for hypomania and normal thyroid and haematological screening give recurrent major depressive disorder rather than a bipolar, chronic or secondary depression.

At moderate severity psychotherapy and medication are equally supported so preference decides, and she has been told psychotherapy is readily available in both formats and has still declined it while asking for something she can start now.

He declines medication and wants a talking therapy, and cognitive behavioural therapy is efficacious across delivery formats, so the access barrier to in-person care is solved by changing the format rather than the modality.

findings: FACTUAL ERROR in distractor rationale B: 'Mammography is cross-sectional imaging of the same persistent mass and answers a structural question, so it competes directly.' Mammography is a two-dimensional projectional radiographic technique, not cross-sectional (tomographic) imaging. The rationale for G2-SURG-02 uses the same phrase correctly of magnetic resonance imaging, so this is not loose shorthand but a wrong statement that would teach a learner a false radiological category.

RATIONALE CONTRADICTS STEM: the key rationale asserts 'Phlegmon is suspected when a history of mastitis worsens into a firm, mass-like area without fluctuance', reproducing the antecedent of CLM-R4-OB-PHLEGMON ('a history of mastitis that worsens into a firm, mass-like area without fluctuance'). The stem positively negates that antecedent: 'she improved promptly on oral antibiotics', 'Her fever settled within the first day', 'there was no point at which she failed to respond to first-line therapy'. The presentation is a non-resolving residual mass, not a worsening one, so the admitted claim's trigger condition is not met by the case the rationale applies it to.

UNSUPPORTED CLAIM in distractor rationale B: 'It belongs where the skin findings of inflammatory breast cancer are present, or where a mass persists after the inflammation has completely resolved and needs a malignancy work-up.' No admitted claim mentions mammography, inflammatory breast cancer, skin thickening, nipple retraction, or the indications for a malignancy work-up. The whole discrimination against the mammography distractor rests on assertions outside the admitted evidence set. The stem features written to defeat it ('The skin is not thickened and the nipple is not retracted') are likewise unbacked.

NOTED, not scored as failure: the stem carries author-voice meta-clauses that pre-perform the elimination for the candidate ('so there was no point at which she failed to respond to first-line therapy', 'so the inflammation has not fully resolved'). These are interpretive tags rather than clinical data. Also noted: option C's qualifier 'without imaging' is an artificial handicap; blind aspiration of a non-fluctuant mass is not real practice, which weakens that option relative to a realistically worded 'ultrasound-guided aspiration'.

Every load-bearing assertion traces to an admitted claim: the key to CLM-R2-SURG-CT ('better in higher body mass index patients ... sensitivity of 90.4 to 100% and specificity of 94%', reproduced accurately as '90.4 to 100 per cent and a specificity of 94 per cent'), distractor A to CLM-R2-SURG-MRI, distractor B to CLM-R2-SURG-YOUNG-MALE-OR, distractor D to CLM-R4-SURG-NONDIAGNOSTIC. Each distractor has a positive stem anchor: 'magnetic resonance imaging are all available immediately' for A, the classic picture plus 'He is haemodynamically stable' for B, 'without guarding or rebound' for D.

OBSERVATION, not a defect: ultrasonography is named as available in the stem but is not an option, even though CLM-R4-SURG-NONDIAGNOSTIC describes a pathway that starts with it. Its absence removes the sharpest test of the declared body-habitus discriminator, since magnetic resonance imaging is actually excluded here by the pregnancy clause rather than by body mass index. The key remains uniquely correct.

OBSERVATION: the stem's parameters (temperature 37.6 degrees Celsius, white cell count 11.8 x 10^9/L, anorexia, vomiting, right lower quadrant tenderness) compute to an Alvarado score of about 7, which some would read as more than intermediate. The stem forecloses this by recording the band explicitly ('the surgical team records the clinical probability of appendicitis as intermediate rather than high'), so no ambiguity survives, but the declared band and the supplied numbers are not perfectly aligned.

'Contrast-enhanced' is a specification beyond CLM-R2-SURG-CT, which says only 'computed tomography'. It is correct standard practice and not decision-critical, so it is not scored as an unsupported claim.

NUMERIC INVERSION, the most serious defect in this set. Distractor rationale B states: 'In the European trials that support it, 53 per cent of patients avoided appendectomy, which means it is offered to a patient who accepts a cross-over and recurrence risk.' The admitted claim CLM-R2-SURG-NONOP says the exact opposite: '53% of patients crossed over to the surgery group within 48 hours'. The rationale takes a crossover-to-surgery rate and reports it as an appendectomy-avoidance rate, inverting the meaning of the only number it cites. The sentence is also self-contradictory as written, since a figure offered as evidence of success is used to justify warning the patient about crossover risk.

The inverted figure is additionally false as medicine: non-operative management trials of uncomplicated appendicitis report appendectomy avoidance well above 53 per cent at 90 days to one year, so '53 per cent of patients avoided appendectomy' misstates both the admitted source and the underlying literature. Scored under factual_correctness, numeric_correctness and evidence_support.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR, option C 'Image-guided percutaneous drainage with antibiotics'. The stem states the computed tomography 'states explicitly that there is no perforation, no free fluid, no abscess and no phlegmon', which positively removes every indication for drainage before the candidate reaches the options. The item's own rationale concedes it: 'The imaging states there is no abscess and no phlegmon, so there is nothing to drain.' Nothing written in the stem draws a candidate toward C.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR, option D 'Antibiotics now with interval appendectomy in six to eight weeks'. Interval appendectomy is indicated after a walled-off phlegmon or abscess settles, and the same explicit CT negations remove that anchor too. The distractor rationale offers only a generic pull ('This is a complete plan that still ends in appendectomy, which is why it reads as a safe compromise'), which is an appeal to option shape rather than to anything in the stem.

CUEING: 'He has been counselled about the options and has expressed no preference and has not been asked to accept any risk of recurrence.' The final clause is not a clinical fact about the patient; it is author-voice bookkeeping inserted solely to disqualify option B, and the rationale then leans on it verbatim ('He has expressed no preference and has not been asked to accept any such risk'). Combined with 'no contraindication to a general anaesthetic or to laparoscopy' and the four explicit CT negations, the stem states each exclusion criterion outright.

REASONING DEMAND: because the stem pre-negates complicated anatomy, operative contraindications and the consent condition for non-operative care, what remains is the single recalled fact that uncomplicated appendicitis in a fit adult is treated by appendectomy. No integration of competing considerations is required.

CRITICAL_FACT_SAFETY: the candidate-facing time window 'in six to eight weeks' in option D rests on no admitted claim. CLM-R2-SURG-DRAINAGE mentions drainage and antibiotics but names no interval. The window happens to match conventional practice, but within this evidence set it is unverified.

RATIONALE CONTRADICTS STEM, distractor C: 'low mood with fatigue, weight change and slowing is exactly the overlap.' The stem lists 'low mood, loss of interest, early morning waking, poor concentration and a five-kilogram weight loss'. It reports neither fatigue nor psychomotor slowing, so the rationale claims an overlap built on two symptoms the case does not contain.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR, option C 'Depressive syndrome due to hypothyroidism'. The stem gives the candidate no positive pull toward it and two positive pushes away: 'Thyroid stimulating hormone ... within normal limits' is stated outright, and the direction of the weight change is wrong, since hypothyroidism characteristically produces weight gain while this patient has 'a five-kilogram weight loss'. An option whose only invitation is the general fact that thyroid disease can mimic depression, with the confirmatory test already reported as normal in the stem, is not competitive.

UNSUPPORTED CLAIM: no admitted claim describes the clinical features of hypothyroidism. CLM-R2-PSY-DDX-MEDICAL says only that 'The differential diagnosis should include psychiatric and nonpsychiatric medical conditions that present with depressive symptoms'. The specific symptom-overlap assertion in rationale C, and the option itself, are therefore unbacked by the evidence supplied with the item.

Correctly handled elsewhere: rationale D reproduces CLM-R2-PSY-PDD faithfully ('Between twenty and thirty per cent ... more than two years'; 'two or more depressive symptoms present for more than two years'), and rationale A reproduces CLM-R2-PSY-BD-MISDX and CLM-R2-PSY-BD-II faithfully. The bipolar II and persistent depressive disorder distractors both carry genuine stem anchors (recurrent discrete episodes at age 34; a four-year span containing two episodes).

UNSUPPORTED CLAIM, distractor rationale B: 'Exercise appears in the same guideline as a treatment with real evidence.' None of the five admitted claims mentions exercise, physical activity or any non-pharmacological, non-psychotherapeutic treatment. The option 'A supervised exercise programme as sole initial treatment' is therefore introduced, and its evidentiary standing asserted, entirely outside the admitted evidence set. This matters because the real-world position is more favourable to exercise than the rationale implies: it is a recognised first-line monotherapy option for mild to moderate depression in Canadian guidance, so the dismissal needs a claim behind it and has none.

One-best-answer holds despite the stem giving a format-flavoured reason for refusal ('she does not wish to attend regular sessions and asks for something she can start now'), because the stem closes the gap explicitly: 'Structured psychotherapy is in fact readily available in her city, in person and digitally, and she has been told so.' She therefore declined the modality with the digital format on the table, which defeats both C and D.

NOTED: options C ('Structured psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy') and D ('Digitally delivered cognitive behavioural therapy') are not mutually exclusive, since D is a delivery format of C. Here both are distractors so no ambiguity reaches the key, and the pair is doing deliberate discriminative work, so this is not scored as a granularity failure in this item. It is fatal in G2-PSY-04, where the same pair straddles the key.

NOTED, bank-level: this item and G2-PSY-04 share three of four options verbatim, an identical lead-in ('Which initial treatment should be offered?'), and an identical clinical frame (moderate major depressive episode, no suicidal ideation, no psychotic features, low safety risk, normal thyroid function and complete blood count). They resolve on different discriminators, so material_redundancy is scored PASS, but the pair reads as a mirrored construction and should not be deployed in the same form.

ONE BEST ANSWER FAILS BY OPTION NESTING. The key is C, 'Digitally delivered cognitive behavioural therapy'. Option A is 'Structured psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy'. Digitally delivered cognitive behavioural therapy is structured psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy, so the keyed answer is an instance of a distractor. A well-prepared candidate who selects A has selected a category that contains the key and is not wrong. Nothing in option A specifies in-person delivery, and the admitted claim CLM-R4-PSY-DIGITAL positively states that the therapy 'appears to be efficacious across formats including individual, group and telephone or digital delivery', which makes digital delivery a subtype of A rather than an alternative to it.

RATIONALE MANUFACTURES THE KEY BY REWRITING THE DISTRACTOR. Rationale A reads: 'Delivered in person it is not available to him: the nearest service is a four-hour drive away with a waiting list of many months and no local therapist is taking referrals, so choosing it in that form leaves him untreated.' The qualifier 'Delivered in person' and 'in that form' are supplied by the rationale, not by the option. The rationale does not explain why the key beats option A as option A is actually written; it defeats a narrowed version of it.

DECISION GRANULARITY: options A and C sit at different grains, a modality and a delivery format of that same modality, while options B and D are whole treatment strategies. The four are not mutually exclusive and not at one decision level.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR, option D 'Combined antidepressant and psychotherapy from the outset'. The stem says 'he has read about antidepressants and does not want to take medication', which removes any pull toward an option containing medication, and it supplies neither of the conditions the guideline attaches to combination ('severe cases of a major depressive episode with high safety risk'), stating the opposite: 'moderate severity ... no suicidal ideation and no psychotic features and his safety risk is low'. The rationale's stated pull is generic efficacy ('on efficacy grounds it is the strongest-sounding option'), not anything written in the stem.

UNSUPPORTED CLAIM, distractor rationale B: 'Exercise is named in the same guideline and needs no therapist.' Neither of the three admitted claims for this item mentions exercise, so the option 'A supervised exercise programme as sole initial treatment' and the assertion about its guideline standing are outside the admitted evidence, exactly as in G2-PSY-03.

The clinical judgement underlying the item is correct: for a moderate episode with low safety risk in a patient refusing medication and unable to reach in-person care, digitally delivered cognitive behavioural therapy is the right offer. The defect is the option set, not the medicine. The fix is to make option A explicitly in-person, or to replace it.
